note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
Job asks, “But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?” It is not found in the land of the living; the depth says it is not in me and the sea says it is not with me. It cannot be gotten for gold, nor silver weighed for its price, nor valued with the gold of Ophir, the onyx or the sapphire, “for the price of wisdom is above rubies.” You will not find God's wisdom deep in the roots of Wakanda; there is no price you can give for it.

Here is where it is found: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.” To get the wisdom of the Most High you take heed to his commandments. The fear of the Lord is understanding that the Lord created us, made us, and can take us out, and that fear is the beginning of wisdom. A good understanding is for all they that do his commandments.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
Everything is in steps, including wisdom. “The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love. The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”

“The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” That is the wisdom Job says cannot be gotten for gold or valued with the gold of Ophir. It is not in the depth or the sea; it is in the fear of the Lord, the first step to being accepted of him, in the performance of the law, and in knowing his omnipotency, that he made us and can take us out.

precepts.text: These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee; the wisdom and understanding of the Lord is for the remnant, not the heathen.
precepts.point: Wisdom and understanding are hid from all living and given only to the few, the remnant of Israel who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations; we fear the Lord like King David, the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who still trembled at God's judgments.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
“Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding? Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living”. It is hid, and given only to the few: “These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee.”

The wisdom and understanding of the Lord is for the remnant, not the heathen. It is hid from all living and given to the remnant of Israel, who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations. God understands the way thereof and knows the place thereof, and he shows it to a few.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
“And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.” Job breaks it down: wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and understanding is to depart from evil.

We fear the Lord like King David: “My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” David was the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who taught his hands to war and could leap a wall, and even he trembled at God's judgments. That trembling is the wisdom that is hid from the eyes of all living.

precepts.why:
Those without the fear of the Lord have no wisdom: “The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.”

That wind ties to the wind of destruction in Job 27, the nuclear destruction, and the winds held back in Revelation. The Lord makes the weight for the winds; the ungodly, who do not depart from evil, are the chaff that wind drives away, while wisdom and understanding stay with the few who fear him.
